sectors.note:
**TL;DR:** Energy and Healthcare lead the market as the only "all-green" sectors, while minor upward rotations in Industrials and Defensives contrast with slipping momentum in Materials and Financials.

Energy (momentum 0.883) and Technology (momentum 0.767) continue to anchor the top of the leaderboard, with Energy and Healthcare (momentum 0.750) standing out as the only two sectors displaying positive performance across all timeframes (week, month, quarter, half, and YTD). A minor upward rotation is underway in Industrials, which gained one spot to reach rank 3, alongside marginal improvements in Consumer Defensive and Communication Services. 

Conversely, cyclical and material sectors are showing signs of exhaustion. Basic Materials fell one spot to rank 4, while Financials slipped to rank 8 despite maintaining a moderate momentum score of 0.583. Consumer Cyclical remains the market's primary laggard, dropping to rank 11 with a weak momentum score of 0.167.

## Strength
* **All-Green Breadth:** Only 2 of 11 sectors—Energy (momentum 0.883, rank 1) and Healthcare (momentum 0.750, rank 6)—are positive across all weekly, monthly, quarterly, semi-annual, and YTD timeframes.
* **Top-Tier Momentum:** Energy (0.883) and Technology (0.767) command the highest overall momentum scores, securing the top two YTD ranks.

## Movers & Momentum
* **Upward Rotation:** Industrials (+1 spot to rank 3, momentum 0.57), Consumer Defensive (+1 spot to rank 7, momentum 0.30), and Communication Services (+1 spot to rank 10, momentum 0.20) were the only sectors to improve their rankings over the last 5 sessions.
* **Rank Declines:** Basic Materials (-1 spot to rank 4, momentum 0.55), Financials (-1 spot to rank 8, momentum 0.58), and Consumer Cyclical (-1 spot to rank 11, momentum 0.17) registered the largest rank drops.
* **Momentum Bottom-Dwellers:** Consumer Cyclical (0.167), Utilities (0.200), and Communication Services (0.200) remain heavily depressed at the bottom of the momentum curve.

## Divergences
* **No Active Divergences:** There are currently no active early-warning signals or fragile "all-green" discrepancies detected across the 11 sector groups.

industries.note:
**TL;DR:** High-momentum technology hardware and oil refining dominate absolute market strength, while a severe collapse in luxury goods contrasts with an emerging defensive rotation into utilities, discount stores, and telecom.

Market leadership remains highly concentrated, with only 19 of 143 industry groups maintaining "all-green" status across weekly, monthly, quarterly, semi-annual, and YTD timeframes. Computer Hardware (0.99 momentum) and Oil & Gas Refining & Marketing (0.98 momentum) lead this elite group. Conversely, consumer discretionary and materials are fading rapidly. Luxury Goods collapsed by 65 spots to rank 111, while Department Stores (-26 spots) and Aluminum (-30 spots) also suffered sharp weekly declines.

An active rotation is underway into defensive and value-oriented sectors. Lodging (+18 spots) and Aerospace & Defense (+17 spots) led the weekly gainers, alongside emerging plays like Discount Stores (+15 spots) and Regulated Gas (+14 spots). Meanwhile, early warning signs are flashing for metals like Copper and Silver, which are slipping in rank despite elevated momentum.

## Strength
* **All-Green Breadth:** Only 19 of 143 groups (13.3%) are positive across all timeframes, anchored by Computer Hardware (0.99 momentum), Oil & Gas Refining & Marketing (0.98 momentum), and Electronics & Computer Distribution (0.89 momentum).
* **Sustained Leadership:** Computer Hardware, Oil & Gas Refining & Marketing, Electronics & Computer Distribution, Staffing & Employment Services, and Biotechnology continue to show sustained top-35 strength across 1-, 3-, and 6-month horizons.
* **Secular Support:** Health Information Services, Diagnostics & Research, and Travel Services join the top-performing cohort as areas of sustained multi-month strength.

## Movers & Momentum
* **Top Gainers:** Lodging (+18 spots to rank 55; 0.59 momentum) and Aerospace & Defense (+17 spots to rank 75; 0.61 momentum) showed the strongest 5-day rank improvements, followed by Discount Stores (+15 spots to rank 71; 0.45 momentum).
* **Top Losers:** Luxury Goods plunged 65 spots to rank 111 (0.24 momentum), while Aluminum (-30 spots to rank 68; 0.45 momentum) and Department Stores (-26 spots to rank 110; 0.48 momentum) also experienced severe weekly drops.
* **Momentum Extremes:** Computer Hardware (0.988, YTD rank 1) and Oil & Gas Refining (0.978, YTD rank 2) lead the market, while Airports & Air Services (0.050) and Advertising Agencies (0.075) remain deeply depressed.

## Divergences
* **Fading Momentum:** Copper (-8 spots, 0.70 momentum), Silver (-8 spots, 0.63 momentum), and Metal Fabrication (-5 spots, 0.75 momentum) are slipping in rank despite elevated momentum, alongside Software - Infrastructure (-5 spots, 0.61 momentum).
* **Emerging Defensives:** Discount Stores (+15 spots, 0.45 momentum), Utilities - Regulated Gas (+14 spots, 0.38 momentum), Utilities - Regulated Electric (+13 spots, 0.45 momentum), and Telecom Services (+13 spots, 0.39 momentum) are climbing rapidly despite low overall momentum scores.
* **Fragile Strength:** Oil & Gas E&P holds an all-green profile but exhibits high vulnerability with a low agreement score of 0.46.
